Definition: Whether the country has an operational Internet Exchange Point (IXP) and its maturity. IXPs enable local internet traffic to be exchanged domestically rather than being routed internationally, reducing latency, costs, and dependence on foreign infrastructure. Critical for local digital ecosystem development.
Comments: No data found after thorough searching
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original source (dlapiperdataprotection.com) is unrelated to IXP presence. PCH and PeeringDB directories confirm Chad has an operational IXP — N'Djamena IX (DJAMIX), established February 2023 and managed by ADETIC (governmental) — with roughly 9-10 peering ASNs and c.82Gbps total capacity recorded. Score changed from 0 (Unknown) to 3 (single IXP with limited participation).
revised_comments: Chad has a single operational Internet Exchange Point, N'Djamena IX (DJAMIX), established in February 2023 and managed by the Agence de Développement des Technologies de l'Information et de la Communication (ADETIC). PeeringDB records around nine to ten participating autonomous systems and roughly 82 Gbps of total peering capacity, indicating limited but active participation typical of an early-stage exchange.

Definition: The availability and presence of major cloud service providers (hyperscale and regional) operating in or serving the country with local or near-local infrastructure. Cloud availability determines access to scalable computing resources for government, business, and startups.
Comments: No data found after thorough searching
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original source (a generic World Bank homepage link) is unrelated to cloud services. Industry reporting shows hyperscale cloud providers (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle, IBM) have deployed only in South Africa, with additional footholds in Nairobi, Lagos and Cairo; none has a presence in Chad. Google's first African cloud region (Johannesburg) only launched in 2026, still distant from Chad. Score changed from 0 (Unknown) to 2 (served remotely from distant regions only).
revised_comments: No hyperscale or regional cloud provider operates a local or near-local availability zone serving Chad. Hyperscaler expansion into Africa remains concentrated in South Africa, Nairobi, Lagos and Cairo, meaning users and businesses in Chad are served remotely from distant cloud regions with correspondingly higher latency.

Definition: Whether the country has enacted legal or regulatory requirements mandating that certain categories of data (personal data, government data, financial data, or critical infrastructure data) be stored within national borders. Central to data sovereignty debates in Africa.
Comments: No data found after thorough searching
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original source (generic World Bank link) unrelated to data localisation. Chad's Law No. 007/PR/2015 on Personal Data Protection (Articles 29-33) restricts cross-border transfer of personal data outside the CEMAC/CEEAC zone absent adequate protection, and requires prior notice to the regulator ANSICE, but does not require that personal, government, financial or critical-infrastructure data be stored within Chad. This is a transfer-adequacy regime, not a data-residency mandate. Score changed from 0 (Unknown) to 1 (no data localisation requirements).
revised_comments: Chad has no data localisation requirement mandating in-country storage of personal, government, financial or critical infrastructure data. Law No. 007/PR/2015 on the Protection of Personal Data instead conditions cross-border transfers of personal data on the receiving country offering an adequate level of protection (or another listed derogation) and requires prior notification to the data protection regulator, ANSICE, rather than requiring data to remain within national borders.

No Tier III or higher commercial colocation facility has yet been identified in the country.

Definition: Whether the government has established dedicated data center infrastructure and/or a government cloud (G-Cloud) strategy for hosting e-government services and public sector data domestically. Critical for data sovereignty and e-government service delivery.
Comments: No data found after thorough searching
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original source (Trading Economics electricity-access page) unrelated to government data centres. Multiple 2026 reports confirm Chad has built a National Data Center under Phase I of the Huawei-implemented, EUR175.1m State Connectivity Infrastructure Modernization Project (PMICE), which received provisional technical reception in late 2025/early 2026; a February 2026 report describes a subsequent security audit/certification process (ADETIC, ANSICE, Techso Group) ahead of formal 'launch', alongside a planned rollout of 100 interconnected government micro data centres. The Chad Connection 2030 national plan sets out the associated e-government/digitalisation strategy. Given ambiguity over whether the centre is yet formally 'operational' pending security certification, this row is flagged for human review to confirm final operational status; best estimate is 3 (basic government data centre operational) rather than 2 (still under construction), since physical construction and technical reception are complete.
revised_comments: The Chadian government has built a National Data Center as Phase I of the State Connectivity Infrastructure Modernization Project (PMICE), a EUR175.1 million initiative implemented with Huawei that also includes 1,200km of national fibre backbone and expanded mobile network coverage. The facility has passed provisional technical reception and is undergoing final security certification, coordinated by ADETIC and the national cybersecurity agency ANSICE, ahead of its formal launch, alongside plans to interconnect 100 government micro data centres. The government's Chad Connection 2030 plan sets out the wider digitalisation and e-government strategy underpinning this infrastructure.

Provides a composite view of the national innovation ecosystem.
Comments: No data found after thorough searching
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown. Value Name differs from the scale label — usually cosmetic.
revision_notes: Original source (RISE energy database) is unrelated to the Global Innovation Index. The GII 2024 covers exactly 133 economies (Niger ranked 132nd, Angola 133rd/last); Chad is not among them, and the World Bank's Chad Digital Economy (DE4A) diagnostic explicitly notes Chad's absence from global entrepreneurship/innovation indexes. This confirms the code 0 (Unknown or n.a. — not included in GII) is correct; no change to Value Code. The 'label_formatting' flag can be cleared as cosmetic only.
revised_comments: Chad is not among the 133 economies ranked in the WIPO Global Innovation Index 2024, and is explicitly noted by the World Bank as absent from global entrepreneurship and innovation indexes, reflecting a lack of the underlying data needed for inclusion rather than a specific ranking.

revised_comments: Chad's tech startup ecosystem is at an emerging stage. Trackers record around 35-39 registered startups, of which about 10 have raised a cumulative $12.8 million in venture/private equity across 15 disclosed funding rounds, concentrated in fintech, e-commerce and digital services and supported by a small number of local hubs (Wenaklabs and Chad Innovation).
